7:- [Slack](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/slack.md): Run MCPJam from Slack — mention the bot to ask about your projects, and appr
ove the actions that spend credits
8:- [MCPJam in Claude](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/claude-connector.md): Connect Claude to your MCPJam account through the host
ed MCP server — projects, saved servers, evals, and user testing
40:- [Migrating to CLI 4.0](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/migration.md): Command-path and flag changes when account-bound mcpjam com
mands moved under mcpjam cloud
53:- [Self-hosted MCPJam](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/self-hosted.md): Point the CLI and SDK at your organization's MCPJam server,
lock it with an IT settings file, and work behind a corporate proxy
82:- [host-compat](https://docs.mcpjam.com/sdk/reference/host-compat.md): API reference for @mcpjam/sdk/host-compat — derive serve
r requirements, evaluate host compatibility, and scan widget bridge usage.
92:- [List run iterations](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/list-run-iterations.md): Per-iteration results: actual
tool calls, structured token usage, and latency. Cursor-paginated.
125:- [Mint a model lease for MCPJam-hosted inference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/mint-a-model-lease-for-mcpj
am-hosted-inference.md): How an SDK eval running OUTSIDE the platform (local dev, CI) uses MCPJam-hosted inference on the organiza
tion's credits, with no provider key of its own. Authenticate like any other `/api/v1` route (typically an `sk_` key).
129:- [Authenticate and record an eval start](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/eval-runs/authenticate-and-record-an-eval-star
t.md): Called by official SDK, CLI and Vitest runners before executing an eval. Requires an organization API key or saved-login be
arer. Records only start metadata, creates no dashboard run, and applies no debit or quota draw. Planned iterations are intent, no
t completed usage. Reuse the runStartId for ret…
143:- [Get the authenticated account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/catalog/get-the-authenticated-account.md): The user be
hind the API key (keys act as their creator, scoped to one organization).
144:- [Read the organization's spend budget](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/catalog/read-the-organizations-spend-budget.md)
: The ceiling on what this organization may spend on MCPJam-billed work — chat, evals, judges and computer time — in the current b
illing window, and how much of it has been spent.
145:- [Set the organization's spend budget](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/catalog/set-the-organizations-spend-budget.md):
Set or replace the ceiling. **Requires organization owner or admin.**
146:- [Remove the organization's spend budget](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/catalog/remove-the-organizations-spend-budget
.md): Leave the organization uncapped. **Requires organization owner or admin.**
147:- [List organizations](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/catalog/list-organizations.md): The organizations the caller belo
ngs to — the source of the `organizationId` that `GET /projects` filters by and `POST /projects` accepts. An API key is bound to o
ne organization and only ever sees that one. Read-only: organization, member, role and billing changes are not part of the public
API.
148:- [List projects](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/catalog/list-projects.md): Projects the caller can access. API keys on
ly ever see projects inside the key's organization.
195:- [List a server's accounts](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/list-a-servers-accounts.md): The accounts t
his server signs in with that you can see: your own personal accounts, or, on a server shared with the project, its project accoun
ts. Another member's personal account never appears. METADATA ONLY: no account response carries a token.
196:- [Get a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/get-a-server-account.md): One account, by id or
name. Another member's personal account answers `404`, the same as a missing one. A name two accounts share answers `409` with `d
etails.code: "account_name_ambiguous"` and both ids in `details.accountIds`.
197:- [Upload tokens to a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/upload-tokens-to-a-server-account.
md): Creates the account (`201`) or replaces its token in place (`200`, same id). A well-formed account id never creates one: an u
nknown id is `404`. Any other reference is a name, and a name no account has creates the account.
198:- [Delete a server account](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/delete-a-server-account.md): Deletes the acc
ount and its stored token. The token's issuer is asked to revoke it where the issuer supports revocation (best effort), which also
invalidates any copy of the same token you hold.
199:- [Rename a server account or make it the default](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/server-accounts/rename-a-server-accou
nt-or-make-it-the-default.md): Rename the account, make it the default, or both; a rename applies first. A name another account on
the server uses answers `409` with `details.code: "account_name_taken"`.
200:- [Import OAuth tokens](https://docs.mcpjam.com/api-reference/oauth/import-oauth-tokens.md): **Deprecated.** Use `PUT /project
s/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/accounts/{account}`. This route uploads to your default account on the server, creating an unname
